identification.title: Refiner's Fire
identification.album: Vineyard Music compilations; later Integrity collections
identification.notes: Written by Brian Doerksen alone, dated 1990 (Wikipedia's list of his songs); copyright line given by listings as Mercy/Vineyard Publishing, administered by Integrity Music; CCLI 426298 (Integrity Worship page). Doerksen was then worship pastor at Langley Vineyard in British Columbia. The list's artist is right. A 35th-anniversary version credits additional contributors and adds a closing tag; the core text is the same. Reviewed as the song, not any one recording. Publication details beyond the 1990 date and CCLI were not found on a page that loaded.

claims.structuralNotes: A short opening refrain, a chorus, a second prayer stanza, then an extended closing section that repeats the chorus, with a tag on the anniversary version. The voice is first person singular throughout, a prayer to God. The opening and second stanza petition for inner cleansing, using the refiner and silver image from Malachi. The chorus states a resolve to be holy and set apart for God. The tag adds readiness to love, serve and care as Christ does. The cross, the resurrection and the Spirit are not named; the song is a prayer for sanctification rather than a statement of the gospel.

claims.claim: God purifies his people as a refiner purifies silver, and the singer asks to be cleansed within.
claims.subject: Sanctification as refining

claims.claim: The singer asks God to search and renew the inner life.
claims.subject: Prayer for a clean heart

claims.claim: The singer resolves to be holy and set apart for God.
claims.subject: Holiness and consecration

claims.claim: The singer offers himself wholly to God as his own.
claims.subject: Self-offering

claims.claim: The singer is ready to love and serve others as Christ does.
claims.subject: Christlike service

strengths.title: A prayer to be made holy
strengths.explanation: The song asks God, not the singer, to do the cleansing, and it frames holiness as being set apart for him. Sanctification is something sought from the refiner.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The call to be holy as God is holy - the aim the chorus resolves toward.

strengths.title: Malachi's refiner at the centre
strengths.explanation: The central image is built on Malachi's picture of God refining his people, with Zechariah and 1 Peter on testing as background. The congregation is taught that trials and cleansing are God's work.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The refiner who purifies silver and cleanses his people - the song's governing picture.

strengths.title: Inner cleansing, not outward show
strengths.explanation: The petitions concern the heart and not performance, in the line of David's prayer for a clean heart.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Create in me a clean heart - the shape of the second stanza's petition.

doctrinesAffirmed: God refines and sanctifies his people
theological.assessment: Nothing false. The resolve in the chorus is a consecration prayer, not a claim to earn salvation, and the singer asks God to do the work. The song is thin on the gospel: it does not name the cross, the resurrection or the grounds on which a sinner is made clean, so it should sit beside songs that do. No independent source assessing its content was found.

strengths.title: Simple and slow
strengths.explanation: A slow prayer with a few repeated phrases that a room learns on first hearing.

strengths.title: Fits a time of consecration
strengths.explanation: Its content suits prayer, response after preaching and times of rededication.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Integrity lists E as a key and notes other keys are available. Check the chorus against the room.

range.key: E (per Integrity Worship page); other keys published
range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The chorus is looped in the long closing section. The repetition is meant for prayerful consecration, but it carries more of the song than the words add.
communal.assessment: Congregational and easy to sing, a slow prayer that a leader can sustain as long as a room wants to pray. The risk is length: the closing section loops the chorus, and the song is better held to the moment of response than extended.

strengths.title: A single image carried through
strengths.explanation: The refiner and silver picture is biblical and widely understood, so the meaning is readable without explanation.

clarity.assessment: Clear. The petitions and the resolve are plain, and the biblical image is easily taken. What a newcomer would not learn is how a sinner is made clean.

synthesis.summary: A first-person prayer to be cleansed and set apart, built on the Malachi picture of a refiner. It asks God to do the work, resolves to live holy and, in the anniversary version, to love and serve like Christ. It does not state the gospel and names no act of God. No false claim found; no independent source on its content was found.
